newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada has and seeks to sell wheat to India - CWB.
newsitem.headline: Canada has and seeks to sell wheat to India - CWB.

text.p: The Canadian Wheat Board has wheat for sale and is in talks with India to secure a sale after that country announced earlier Thursday it is seeking to import for the first time in four years.
"I just talked to our sales guy for India and he said we are talking to them and we have grain for sale," CWB spokeswoman Tracey Thompson told Reuters.
Indian Food Minister Devendra Prasad Yadav said India would import 2.0 million tonnes of wheat in fiscal 1996/97 (April/March) to augment dometic supplies and check rising prices.
The last time it imported that much wheat was in 1991/92.
The commercial attache at the High Commission of India in Ottawa declined comment.
Grain trade sources, however, said the CWB will probably sell little, if any, of the 2.0 million tonnnes India needs.
"What they want is so quick the Board can't do it. They want December shipment for January arrival. Australia's the only one logistically able to do that," a trade source said.
"We're pretty well sold out now until February for shipment which is really, for India, March arrival," he added.
Australia likely sold 1.0 million tonnes of wheat to India already, partly due to its proximity and US$5 a tonne freight advantage over Vancouver wheat shipments, another source said.
"The price of wheat here would have to be below the (CWB) initial price (a government partial payment) to compete, we think the numbers are sub US$150 FOB Vancouver," he said.
Benchmark No1 Canada Western Red Spring Wheat's initial price is C$190 a tonne, in-store Vancouver, or US$139.78.
The CWB sold 102,000 tonnes of wheat to India in marketing year 1991/92 (Aug/July) 449,000 tonnes in 1992/93, CWB spokeswoman Deanna Allen said.
The CWB held a 21 percent share of the world's milling wheat market in crop year 1994/95 (Aug/July).
